speaker.name: Kelbin
colour_lines: Muleteers sing as they cross so the ones ahead will hear them in the cloud.
The Windward Waystation keeps odd hours, so knock twice, wait, and do not take it personally.
own_lines: I was brought up in a mill town where everyone knew everyone's business.
I carried letters for a grain merchant. I know most of the lanes between the towns around here.
I walked alone to the nearest great city at fifteen. It took eleven days and one very lucky ride on a hay cart.
I do the small job as well as the great one. Nobody can tell the difference until it matters.
I have a neighbour I have been competing with for thirty years. I would be lost without them.
I want this errand finished and a whole day of sleep after. In that order, if luck allows.
Muleteers sing as they cross so the ones ahead will hear them in the cloud.
The Windward Waystation keeps odd hours, so knock twice, wait, and do not take it personally.
Most of what is said about the guard is probably exaggerated, but not all of it.
The way to the Windward Waystation runs through the Windward Pass, and I would not linger there.
I need the iron coffer carried to the Windward Waystation, and there is no one else I can ask.
Tomas is a watch sergeant at the Windward Waystation.
I swore to an old friend that the iron coffer would reach Tomas.
Tonight I may not keep my word.
My friend is gone now.
This is all I have left of the promise, and I won't see it lost.
Thank you.
Tomas will be at the Windward Waystation.
Get me there, and my promise is kept.
Thank you.
We can catch our breath here.
I carried the iron coffer once before, as a child, walking beside my grandmother. I was too small to know what it meant.
